subject: EU data residency & configurable retention - implementation Q&A
messages:
From: security@acme-corp.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Sun, 18 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data residency / retention Qs for Redwood - Acme evaluation

Hi Karthik,

Following our demo last week, the security team at Acme has a short set of follow-up questions as we consolidate vendor assessments. High level: we need to know whether Redwood can (a) guarantee that customer content lives only in EU regions for EU customers and (b) support configurable retention windows per workspace (including per-environment overrides for staging vs prod).

Specific asks:
- Can you confirm region-of-storage options today and any timelines for adding more EU availability zones?
- Is retention configurable per workspace? Can default retention be set to 30/90/365 days and overridden per project?
- How is deletion implemented (hard delete vs logical delete)? What evidence do you provide to customers that data was deleted?
- Any impacts to caching, embeddings, or logs when short retention windows are enforced?

We attached our vendor RFI (ACME_RFI_Attachments.zip) with the detailed checklist — please reply with short answers and an expected timeline if the feature is not GA.

Thanks,
Jamie Brown
Senior Security Analyst, Acme Corp
[attachment: ACME_RFI_Attachments.zip]
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: security@acme-corp.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 18 May 2025 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data residency / retention Qs for Redwood - Acme evaluation

Hi Jamie — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Grace (Product) and Evelyn (Engineering) to confirm specifics and timelines; copying procurement so they have visibility.

Short answers up front:
- Region storage: We currently offer EU-hosted tenants in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1; we can pin model storage and metadata to EU-only for an account (GA).
- Retention: Per-workspace retention knobs are in the product backlog; current hosted defaults are 365 days with manual deletion options.
- Deletion: We support logical deletion now; hard delete (purge with verifiable audit record) is an ETA item for customers requiring shorter SLAs.
- Caching/logs: Short retention will require changes in KV cache eviction and embedding persistence — likely small perf trade-offs.

Grace/Evelyn — can you supply a one-paragraph feasibility summary and a target timeline we can share with Acme (preferably with conservative ETA)? Also attaching the RFI they included.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — quick product read:

Summary and proposed customer-facing position:
- Residency: EU-only tenancy is GA; we can document and sign data residency commitments for accounts scoped to EU regions.
- Retention controls: We have a roadmap item to provide per-workspace retention presets (30/90/365 + custom) and environment-level overrides. Proposed rollout: 1) admin UI + API to set retention at workspace level (Q3 2025 beta) 2) hard-delete purge tool with audit-proof deletion receipts (Q4 2025).
- Coverage: This will include primary storage and embeddings persistence; logs/audit retention is separate and will be configurable via the console (note: compliance team required to confirm minimum retention for audit purposes).

Ask to engineering: please confirm the scope below and call out any blockers or dependencies (KMS, cross-region replication, S3 lifecycle hooks, and embedding store semantics). I attached a short proposal and rough wireframe for the UI.

Attachments: retention-proposal-v1.pdf

Grace O'Connor

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Data residency / retention Qs for Redwood - Acme evaluation

Thanks for the summary — engineering notes below. High level: feasible but non-trivial.

Technical considerations:
- Residency: For EU-only accounts we must ensure control plane metadata and object storage are pinned; this is already in place for new EU tenants, but retrofitting existing accounts will require migration tooling (estimated 4-6 engineer-weeks per migration path).
- Retention config: Adding a per-workspace retention config is straightforward (API + UI) ~2-3 sprints. The hard part is guaranteeing cryptographic-proof hard deletes: we need a purge pipeline that removes objects, invalidates KV caches, and produces a signed deletion receipt. Building that end-to-end is ~3-4 sprints and requires KMS/HSM integration work for receipts.
- Embeddings/cache: Short retention (e.g., 30 days) increases churn in our embeddings store and will reduce cache hit rates; we should add intelligent TTL-aware batching to mitigate token-cost impact — that's another 2-sprint enhancement.
- Compliance: We need input from Neha on minimum audit retention windows for logs and whether we can allow customers to opt into shorter app-data retention while retaining longer audit logs.

Risks/dependencies:
- KMS key provisioning for per-account/deletion receipts (security must sign receipts).
- S3 lifecycle vs immediate purge semantics for deletion requests (legal may require immediate purges).
- Migration playbook for existing accounts (ops runbook + runbook automation).

Suggested next steps: prioritize EPIC ENG-2987 (retention & purge receipts) and PRD-1210 (workspace retention config). Recommend a conservative external ETA: beta for workspace retention config in Q3 2025; hard-delete + signed receipts targeted for Q4 2025.

Evelyn Hart
Engineering Manager, Platform Services
Redwood Inference

Jamie — looping back with an internal summary. Key points to share with your stakeholders:
- EU data residency: GA for new EU accounts; migration path available for existing accounts (ops runbook + estimated effort).
- Per-workspace retention: product has this on the roadmap — conservative ETA: beta Q3 2025.
- Hard-delete + signed deletion receipts: targeted Q4 2025 — this will require KMS integration and is treated as a priority for customers with strict deletion SLAs.
- Short retention caveat: there will be measurable effects on embedding/cache hit rates; engineering plans mitigations but cost/latency trade-offs exist.

Neha from security will follow up on acceptable audit-log retention defaults and any contract language we should use for deletion guarantees.

Would you like a short one-page summary + timeline we can share with Acme's procurement and security teams? We can deliver that by EOD Tuesday if that helps.
